blocks.h2: Why McHenry Sewer Lines Need Regular Cleaning

tiles.body: A low spot collects debris. Cleaning it on a schedule prevents backups while you plan a repair.
Hard water leaves deposits that narrow drain lines over time.
Roots return to the same joints every year.
A backup on new flooring costs far more than a cleaning.

blocks.intro: In July 2017, heavy rain and Fox River flooding led the state to declare McHenry County a disaster area. Wet seasons put every sewer line to the test.

items.h3: Clear Lines Handle Wet Seasons Better
items.body: A line that's partly blocked has less room when groundwater and heavy use add to the flow.
Clean before spring rain and snowmelt, when lines carry the most.
If you have a backflow valve or an [overhead sewer system](/mchenry/overhead-sewer-systems), we'll test it on the same visit.

blocks.h2: What a Maintenance Visit Can (and Can't) Fix
blocks.intro: A maintenance visit is built around prevention, not repair. Here's where the line falls:
head: Included in a Maintenance Visit
Needs a Different Service
rows: A camera inspection to check your line's current condition
An active sewage backup. Likely fix: [Emergency Plumbing](/mchenry/emergency-plumbing)
Catching early root growth or wear before it becomes a bigger problem
A cracked or collapsed pipe. Likely fix: [Sewer Repair](/mchenry/sewer-repair)
A light interior clean as part of the visit
A heavy clog that needs full clearing. Likely fix: [Sewer Rodding](/mchenry/sewer-rodding) or [Hydro Jetting](/mchenry/hydro-jetting)
An honest assessment of what your line needs next
A line at the end of its lifespan. Likely fix: [Trenchless Sewer Repair](/mchenry/trenchless-sewer-repair)
blocks.note: If your line needs more than a checkup, we'll tell you exactly what and why. No surprise upsells.

blocks.h2: Sewer Maintenance Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: How often should my sewer line be cleaned?
items.preview: Based on what's in it. Roots usually mean once a year.
items.answer: It depends on the cause. Roots usually mean yearly cleaning. A sag may need cleaning every year or two until it's fixed. A clean line may only need an occasional camera check.

items.q: Can regular cleaning replace a repair?
items.preview: It can manage the problem. It doesn't fix a broken pipe.
items.answer: Cleaning manages roots, grease and debris. It doesn't fix a sag, crack or collapse. If the camera shows damage, we'll explain your repair options.

items.q: Does cleaning help during high water?
items.preview: It helps your line carry more, but it can't stop an overloaded sewer.
items.answer: A clean line drains faster. If the public sewer is overloaded and pushing back, you need protection like a backflow valve or [overhead sewer](/mchenry/overhead-sewer-systems).

items.q: Is sewer cleaning part of the No Drip Club?
items.preview: The No Drip Club includes regular maintenance visits.
items.answer: The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club/) brings a plumber to your home for regular maintenance. Ask us how it applies to your sewer line.

items.q: How much does sewer line cleaning cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the line. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on whether your line needs rodding, jetting or a camera check, and on access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
